disclaimer: Fictional sample company. Generated data for demonstration, not measurements.

assumptions.note: Request volumes, per-request prices by team and budgets are illustrative assumptions for the sample company. Spend prevented by the anomaly pause is the paused job's hourly rate times the hours it would have run until someone read the invoice (estimated, not measured).

incidents.handled: Each failed attempt fell through to gpt-4.1-mini within the same request; members saw about a second of extra latency and no errors.
Circuit breaker opened after 3 failures; traffic fell back to Claude Haiku. 99.6% of affected requests still succeeded.
Breaker half-open probes recovered the route; no member-facing errors.

notable.title: Twelve minutes of Anthropic overload, no member-facing errors
notable.detail: claude-haiku-4-5 returned 529s from 2:05 to 2:17 pm; smart-fast requests fell back to gpt-4.1-mini within the same call.

notable.title: Contractor key blocked from Sonnet-class models
notable.detail: A vendor's code-assistant key asked for claude-sonnet-4-5; the contractors policy denied it and the request fell to an allowed alias.

notable.title: Runaway fraud-scoring batch paused at 10.2x its baseline
notable.detail: A retry loop multiplied requests; anomaly detection paused the key within the hour. Estimated spend prevented: $2,310 before the next business day.

notable.title: Provider incident absorbed by fallback
notable.detail: 47 minutes of OpenAI errors; the member assistant and online banking chat kept answering through Claude Haiku.

notable.title: September showback sent to department heads
notable.detail: CSV export by team and app; risk analytics came in 9% under budget after moving dispute triage onto the on-prem model.

notable.title: Regulated workloads pinned to on-prem models
notable.detail: BSA and dispute-evidence prompts now route only to the on-prem Llama deployment; fallback can't reach a cloud provider.
